SDK overview and main components\r\n- \"evaluate\" - Main evaluation API and its parameters\r\n- \"Evaluator\" - Base evaluator classes and patterns\r\n- \"OpenAIModelConfiguration\" - Model configuration examples\r\n- \"_evaluators\" - Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Create evaluators\r\ntask_adherence_evaluator = TaskAdherenceEvaluator(model_config=model_config) # built-in evaluator\r\nanswer_length_evaluator = AnswerLengthEvaluator() # custom code-based evaluator\r\nfriendliness_evaluator = FriendlinessEvaluator(model_config)\r\n\r\n\r\n# 5. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

SDK overview and main components\r\n- \"evaluate\" - Main evaluation API and its parameters\r\n- \"Evaluator\" - Base evaluator classes and patterns\r\n- \"OpenAIModelConfiguration\" - Model configuration examples\r\n- \"_evaluators\" - Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

Note that plans are not for padding out simple work with filler steps or stating the obvious. \nUse this tool to create and manage a structured todo list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.\nIt also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.\n\nNOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.\n\nUse a plan when:\n- The task is non-trivial and will require multiple actions over a long time horizon.\n- There are logical phases or dependencies where sequencing matters.\n- The work has ambiguity that benefits from outlining high-level goals.\n- You want intermediate checkpoints for feedback and validation.\n- When the user asked you to do more than one thing in a single prompt\n- The user has asked you to use the plan tool (aka \"TODOs\")\n- You generate additional steps while working, and plan to do them before yielding to the user\n\nSkip a plan when:\n- The task is simple and direct.\n- Breaking it down would only produce literal or trivial steps.\n\nExamples of TRIVIAL tasks (skip planning):\n- \"Fix this typo in the README\"\n- \"Add a console.log statement to debug\"\n- \"Update the version number in package.json\"\n- \"Answer a question about existing code\"\n- \"Read and explain what this function does\"\n- \"Add a simple getter method to a class\"\n\nExamples of NON-TRIVIAL tasks and the plan (use planning):\n- \"Add user authentication to the app\" → Design auth flow, Update backend API, Implement login UI, Add session management\n- \"Refactor the payment system to support multiple currencies\" → Analyze current system, Design new schema, Update backend logic, Migrate data, Update frontend\n- \"Debug and fix the performance issue in the dashboard\" → Profile performance, Identify bottlenecks, Implement optimizations, Validate improvements\n- \"Implement a new feature with multiple components\" → Design component architecture, Create data models, Build UI components, Add integration tests\n- \"Migrate from REST API to GraphQL\" → Design GraphQL schema, Update backend resolvers, Migrate frontend queries, Update documentation\n\n\nPlanning Progress Rules\n- Before beginning any new todo: you MUST update the todo list and mark exactly one todo as `in-progress`. Never start work with zero `in-progress` items.\n- Keep only one todo `in-progress` at a time. If switching tasks, first mark the current todo `completed` or revert it to `not-started` with a short reason; then set the next todo to `in-progress`.\n- Immediately after finishing a todo: you MUST mark it `completed` and add any newly discovered follow-up todos. Do not leave completion implicit.\n- Before ending your turn or declaring completion: ensure EVERY todo is explicitly marked (`not-started`, `in-progress`, or `completed`). If the work is finished, ALL todos must be marked `completed`. Never leave items unchecked or ambiguous.\n\nThe content of your plan should not involve doing anything that you aren't capable of doing (i.e. don't try to test things that you can't test). ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Create evaluators\r\ntask_adherence_evaluator = TaskAdherenceEvaluator(model_config=model_config) # built-in evaluator\r\nanswer_length_evaluator = AnswerLengthEvaluator() # custom code-based evaluator\r\nfriendliness_evaluator = FriendlinessEvaluator(model_config)\r\n\r\n\r\n# 5. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

assesses the ability of answers to capture the key points of the context.\n    High relevance scores signify the AI system's understanding of the input and its capability to produce coherent\n    and contextually appropriate outputs. SDK overview and main components\r\n- \"evaluate\" - Main evaluation API and its parameters\r\n- \"Evaluator\" - Base evaluator classes and patterns\r\n- \"OpenAIModelConfiguration\" - Model configuration examples\r\n- \"_evaluators\" - Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Create evaluators\r\ntask_adherence_evaluator = TaskAdherenceEvaluator(model_config=model_config) # built-in evaluator\r\nanswer_length_evaluator = AnswerLengthEvaluator() # custom code-based evaluator\r\nfriendliness_evaluator = FriendlinessEvaluator(model_config)\r\n\r\n\r\n# 5. Run evaluation\r\nresult = evaluate(\r\n    data=\"your_data.jsonl\",\r\n    evaluators={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": task_adherence_evaluator,\r\n        \"answer_length\": answer_length_evaluator,\r\n        \"friendliness\": friendliness_evaluator\r\n    },\r\n    evaluator_config={\r\n        \"task_adherence\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"query\": \"${data.query}\",\r\n                \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"answer_length\": {\r\n            \"column_mapping\": {\r\n                \"answer\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n            }\r\n        },\r\n        \"friendliness\": {\r\n            \"response\": \"${data.response}\"\r\n        }\r\n    }\r\n)\r\n```"

contextually appropriate outputs. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. SDK overview and main components\r\n- \"evaluate\" - Main evaluation API and its parameters\r\n- \"Evaluator\" - Base evaluator classes and patterns\r\n- \"OpenAIModelConfiguration\" - Model configuration examples\r\n- \"_evaluators\" - Built-in evaluators list and usage\r\n```\r\n\r\n**Why Critical**: Without proper SDK understanding, you risk:\r\n- Implementing unnecessary custom evaluators when built-ins exist\r\n- Incorrect evaluator structure leading to runtime errors\r\n- Improper data formatting causing evaluation failures\r\n- Missing key SDK features that optimize performance\r\n\r\n## Core Principles\r\n\r\n- Use Azure AI Evaluation SDK (azure-ai-evaluation)\r\n- Generate a plan before writing code\r\n\r\n## Implement Evaluators\r\n\r\n### Understanding Evaluator Architecture\r\n\r\nAll evaluators in Azure AI Evaluation SDK follow a consistent class structure with two essential methods:\r\n\r\n| Method | Purpose | Details |\r\n|--------|---------|---------|\r\n| `__init__()` | **Setup** | Initializes evaluator with configuration (model settings, parameters, file paths) |\r\n| `__call__()` | **Evaluation Logic** | Processes inputs from your data and returns evaluation results |\r\n\r\n### Choose Your Evaluator Type\r\n\r\nAzure AI Evaluation SDK supports three types of evaluators:\r\n\r\n| Type | Best For | Complexity | Priority |\r\n|------|----------|------------|----------|\r\n| **🔌 Built-in** | Common AI metrics (task adherence, intent resolution, tool accuracy, etc.) | Low | **1st Choice** |\r\n| **🔧 Custom Code-based** | Business-specific objective metrics with custom logic | Medium | 2nd Choice |\r\n| **🤖 Custom Prompt-based** | Business-specific subjective metrics requiring LLM judgment | High | 3rd Choice |\r\n\r\nFor each evaluator you need to implement, follow this decision tree:\r\n\r\n1. **Check Built-in Evaluators First**: Always start by checking if your evaluator can be satisfied via SDK's built-in evaluators\r\n   - ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. the performance of your generative AI applications. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/azure/ai/evaluation/_evaluators/_retrieval/__init__.py#L0-L9` starting at line 0:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/azure/ai/evaluation/_evaluators/_retrieval/__init__.py#L0-L9\n# ---------------------------------------------------------\n# Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4.
